Dear Journal,
As far as I'm concerned this is the best time in my life!
I received my official transcript and Restaurant Management certificate and I aced each course! By this time next year, I will have found a restaurant location. I will have started designing it and I will have completed my business plan. Also, I will have found some serious investors. Until that time I relish each moment, each step towards the future.

My life coaching and mindfulness practice gave me the awareness that presence is valuable! In the last meditation session, I wrote this:
I am peering into my future. I visualize myself as the warm rays of the rising sun over the horizon of my life. When I have reached a level of contentment in my career and personal life, I will have more to do. If I imagine opening up to all possibilities, I will become non-judgmental of myself and others. The future is coming in waves just like the present.

The vision of myself in the future is what I see now: I will be holding my child near a deep green forest, and I will be tasting new recipes in the crystal blue kitchen of my own restaurant. I will be lying on the side of a grassy hill quietly reading with my partner. I know that as I get older I will have begun to reap the benefits of my hard work and I won't have forgotten about the truth within me. Before I can see further into the future, I will accept mindfulness. As soon as I accept it, I will gain peace of mind.

This practice must be my priority. I have to remember to do it, but I must not force it. I mustn't stand in my own way. I must recognize self-doubt and let it be.
At any rate, I have to love, accept and nurture my soul.

Future Continuous and Future Perfect Tense: Review

You use the Future Continuous to talk about something that will be in progress in the future.
You use the Future Perfect to talk about something that will be finished by a particular time in the future.
I will be working at 4 p.m. tomorrow.
The person will start work at some point in the future and be working at 4 p.m. It is not clear when the person will stop working.
There are two other ways to use the Future Continuous tense:
• You can use the Future Continuous to show a long action will be interrupted by a shorter action in the future .
Structure: </br><ul>will + be + present participle of the verb

Example:
    I will be holding my child near a deep green forest, when someone appears in front of me.
• You use the Future Continuous to express the idea that two actions will be happening simultaneously for the same amount of time. You can use two Future Continuous actions in one sentence.
Structure: </br><ul>am/is/are + going to be + present participle

Example:
    I am going to be lying on the side of a grassy hill and my husband is going to be looking after the kids.

The Future Perfect tense is similar to the Present Perfect tense, but instead of your viewpoint being in the present, it is in the future.
The Future Perfect is also used to express certainty of a future event being completed or to convey a strong opinion about a future event.
You can use expressions like I'm sure ... or I really think ... to express certainty with the Future Perfect.

The Future Perfect has two forms:
will have + past participle, or
am/is/are + going to have + past participle

Example:
    By this time next year, I'll have found the perfect restaurant location.
    I'm sure I'll have found some serious investors.
I will have found a restaurant location.
I will have started designing it and  I will have completed my business plan.
Also, I will have found some serious investors.

You use the modals must and have (got) to to express necessity in the present and in the past
You use the negative forms of the modals need to and have to to express absence of necessity in the present.
Must refers to a necessary condition that comes from the subject and may be directed at the subject or the person the subject is talking to or about. It is used to show a strong necessity.
I must recognize self-doubt and let it be.
Have (got) to expresses obligation that comes from outside, such as rules and regulations over which the subject has no control. It is used to express necessity in a lower degree than with must.
I have to accept love and nurture my soul.
Absence of necessity is expressed often by using the negative form of have to. You use mustn't less often than have to.
I don't have to worry so much all the time.

You can only express necessity in the past with the modal have to.
Structure:
    subject + had to + infinitive

Example:
I had to make some pretty big changes in my life recently
To show the absence of necessity in the past, you use the structure:
Luckily, I didn't have to renew my Restaurant Management certificate!
Absence of necessity can also be expressed by negative form of need.
This practice must be my priority.
I have to remember to do it, but I must not force it.
I mustn't stand in my own way.
